These values are conventions observed across Indian merchant SDKs, not a
published spec, and apps change them between releases. `androidConfidence`
and `iosConfidence` each record whether that platform's own value has been
confirmed on a real device -- tracked separately because the two are
verified independently, often on different hardware at different times, and
one being confirmed says nothing about the other. `unverified` entries (the
default when the field is omitted) are plausible but untested, and are
excluded from getUpiAppTargets unless explicitly asked for. See
docs/verify-upi-targets.md for how to promote one.

Coverage here is much narrower than the handle map in src/apps.ts, and the
gap is not an oversight. A handle is published data; a deep-link target has
to be tested. Detecting an app wrongly is cosmetic. Sending a payer into a
link that silently drops the amount is a failed payment.
Android package names come from Play Store listings, which are self-proving:
the `id=` parameter in the URL is the package name. There is no equivalent
for iOS schemes -- they are published nowhere, and the third-party lists that
collect them have been wrong about apps in this very table, so no iOS scheme
is added without a device confirming it.
An entry with only an androidPackage is normal and useful: the Android
branch of buildUpiAppLink works from it, while iOS callers fall through to
the QR. Nothing here appears in getUpiAppTargets for a given platform until
that platform's own confidence is `established`.
